srp_violations.description: Acts as service locator, singleton, state machine, and netcode event dispatcher simultaneously. Manages bootstrapping via reflection (TryInvokeInstanceMethod) to call SteamBootstrap and SteamLobbyNetcode, coupling it tightly to Steam-specific lifecycle.
evidence: Calls methods on other MonoBehaviours by name via reflection
Exposes multiple services (Config, PlayerRegistry, SceneFlow, IdentityProvider)

srp_violations.description: Combines session phase state machine, network scene loading orchestration, player teleportation logic, and spawn point resolution into a single NetworkBehaviour.
evidence: Finds and resolves NetSpawnPointGroup components at runtime
Exposes duplicate overloads for same operations (CanStartRun, ReturnToLobby)

srp_violations.description: Orchestrates high-level game flow (start run / return to hub) but also directly controls elevator, scene callback subscription, and coroutine sequencing.
Handles voice capture, encoding, network transport (send/receive), buffer management, and player lookup all in one MonoBehaviour.
evidence: Manages multiple byte and float buffers inline
Relays voice data on server via named-message handlers
Finds player objects by clientId at runtime

srp_violations.description: Handles both movement logic (walk, sprint, crouch) and physics (gravity application) and crouching animation via coroutine. Implements IControlable, making it both a data receiver and a physics actor.
evidence: HandleMovement + ApplyGravity + CrouchStandTransition all in one class
Stores both input state and physics state (velocity)

code_smells.description: NetLobbyReadyPlatform and NetReadyPlatformGate are nearly identical: both manage overlap counting (Dictionary<ulong, int>), countdown logic, and AllReadyConfirmedServer state. One appears to be a copy-paste of the other with minor differences.
code_smells.suggestion: Merge into a single configurable component or extract shared logic into a base class / helper.

code_smells.description: NetGameRoot uses System.Reflection (TryInvokeInstanceMethod) to invoke methods on SteamBootstrap and SteamLobbyNetcode by string name. This is fragile, bypasses type safety, and makes refactoring dangerous.
code_smells.suggestion: Define interfaces (e.g., INetBootstrapper, INetLobbyController) and have SteamBootstrap/SteamLobbyNetcode implement them. Inject via typed fields.

code_smells.description: NetGameSession has 30+ methods, manages multiple state machines, and handles scene loading, player teleportation, and spawn point resolution. It is the largest and most complex class in the project.
code_smells.suggestion: Extract teleportation logic into NetPlayerTeleporter, spawn point resolution into NetSpawnResolver, and keep NetGameSession as a thin orchestrator.

code_smells.description: Scene names (Tavern, Dungeon) appear both as [SerializeField] defaults on NetGameSession AND in NetGameConfig. There is risk of divergence and no single source of truth.
code_smells.suggestion: Remove scene name fields from NetGameSession and always read from NetGameConfig. Or use SceneReference assets.

code_smells.description: Default buffer sizes in NetSteamProximityVoiceChat are hardcoded inline (8192, 16384, 24000) rather than named constants or config values.
code_smells.suggestion: Extract to private const or move to NetSteamVoiceConfig.

code_smells.description: NetFpsPlayerAdapter and NetLocalCameraEnforcer overlap in responsibility: both disable other cameras on network spawn. This split ownership makes behaviour hard to predict.
code_smells.suggestion: Decide on a single authoritative component for camera ownership enforcement and remove the duplicate logic from the other.

code_smells.description: Multiple classes expose static Instance singletons (NetGameRoot, NetGameSession, NetRunSessionController, NetSteamProximityVoiceChat). In a networked game this risks stale references across scene loads.
code_smells.suggestion: Prefer dependency injection via serialized references or a lightweight service locator scoped to the network session lifetime.

code_smells.description: Several scripts are in the global namespace instead of a project namespace: CharacterMovement, FirstPersonCamera, HeadBobbing, PlayerInputHandler, IControlable, NetGameSession, MouthBlendshapeTalkAnimator.
code_smells.suggestion: Move all scripts under a consistent namespace (e.g., HuntGame or DungeonSteakhouse).

code_smells.description: NetGameConfig and NetSteamVoiceConfig expose all fields as public instead of using [SerializeField] private with properties. This allows any code to mutate config at runtime.
code_smells.suggestion: Use [field: SerializeField] with auto-properties, or private fields with [SerializeField] and public read-only properties.

code_smells.description: CharacterMovement implements IControlable.SetLookInput but CharacterMovement itself does not perform camera rotation — that is handled by FirstPersonCamera. The method body likely does nothing or is unused.
code_smells.suggestion: Either remove SetLookInput from IControlable or split IControlable into IMovable and ILookable.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Replace reflection in NetGameRoot with typed interfaces
refactoring_suggestions.description: TryInvokeInstanceMethod uses string-based reflection to call Host/LeaveLobby on SteamBootstrap and SteamLobbyNetcode. This is the most fragile pattern in the codebase. Define INetBootstrapper { void Initialize(); void Shutdown(); } and INetLobbyController { void Host(); void LeaveLobby(); } and inject typed references.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Merge NetLobbyReadyPlatform into NetReadyPlatformGate
refactoring_suggestions.description: Both classes are near-identical. NetLobbyReadyPlatform adds no significant differentiation over NetReadyPlatformGate. Remove NetLobbyReadyPlatform entirely and replace all usages with NetReadyPlatformGate configured to HubOnly mode.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Decompose NetGameSession — extract teleportation and spawn resolution
refactoring_suggestions.description: Create NetPlayerSpawnResolver (finds NetSpawnPointGroup, returns position/rotation for a clientId) and NetPlayerTeleporter (executes deferred teleport coroutines). NetGameSession becomes a thin FSM that delegates to these.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Establish a single source of truth for scene names
refactoring_suggestions.description: Remove lobbySceneName / runSceneName from NetGameSession. Always read from NetGameConfig. Optionally replace string scene names with SceneReference assets (Addressables) to get compile-time safety.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Decide camera enforcement authority: remove overlap between NetFpsPlayerAdapter and NetLocalCameraEnforcer
refactoring_suggestions.description: Both components disable other cameras on spawn. Pick one as the canonical camera enforcer (NetLocalCameraEnforcer is more robust with its scene-load re-enforcement) and remove DisableOtherEnabledCameras / DisableOtherAudioListeners from NetFpsPlayerAdapter.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Move global-namespace scripts into project namespaces
refactoring_suggestions.description: CharacterMovement, FirstPersonCamera, HeadBobbing, PlayerInputHandler, IControlable, NetGameSession, and MouthBlendshapeTalkAnimator all lack a namespace. Add HuntGame or HuntGame.Player namespaces to prevent future name collisions.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Split IControlable into IMovable and ILookable
refactoring_suggestions.description: CharacterMovement implements SetLookInput despite not doing camera rotation. Separating the interface removes a misleading contract and allows future controllers that only need movement or only need look.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Extract voice buffer constants into NetSteamVoiceConfig
refactoring_suggestions.description: Magic numbers 8192, 16384, and 24000 in NetSteamProximityVoiceChat should be named constants or driven by NetSteamVoiceConfig to allow tuning without code changes.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Make NetGameConfig and NetSteamVoiceConfig fields read-only from outside
refactoring_suggestions.description: All public fields on these ScriptableObjects are writable at runtime, risking accidental mutation. Change to private [SerializeField] fields exposed through read-only properties.

refactoring_suggestions.title: Audit and reduce singleton usage
refactoring_suggestions.description: NetGameRoot, NetGameSession, NetRunSessionController, and NetSteamProximityVoiceChat all use static Instance. In multiplayer with scene reloads this is error-prone. Consider a session-scoped service container (plain C# class registered in Awake) or Unity's new dependency injection patterns.
